notes: SmolLM3-3B.litertlm as uploaded to litert-community/SmolLM3-3B on 2026-10-06 (Hub commit af261561): graph rewrite of the previous Hub file (KV-cache writes -> odml.cache_update, attention products -> odml.runtime_bmm, param_tensor input, broadcast mask add) plus one copied 16-token prefill signature; the weights are byte-identical to the previous file (sha256 f9aa844c27f5...), which this upload replaced. Built and measured by the litertlm-convert GPU graph re-ship lane (rounds 1-21). Mac gate of this file (round 19, litertlm-convert gpu_reship_work/results/ship_verify): 6/6 points — weights and every other section byte-identical to the previous file, tflite CPU outputs bit-identical, litert-lm CPU answers 9/9 byte-identical, GPU (WebGPU) fully delegated with fp32 activations 9/9 byte-identical; GPU fp16 (the default) final answers 7/8 against 7/8 without the 16-token signature. Galaxy S26 GPU gate (round 20, Session path, greedy): 4/4 questions, long prompt correct, the same points as the file without the 16-token signature on the same phone. Previous file on the same Mac in the same lock window (litert-lm 0.17.1, same flags): gpu p256 d256: decode 76.99 tok/s, prefill 1413.98 tok/s, TTFT 0.2052 s; gpu p16 d32: decode 74.47 tok/s, prefill 88.27 tok/s, TTFT 0.2047 s; cpu p256 d256: decode 24.41 tok/s, prefill 461.14 tok/s, TTFT 1.9967 s; cpu p16 d32: decode 11.9 tok/s, prefill 28.49 tok/s, TTFT 2.0327 s. Galaxy S26 rows: Google's prebuilt litert_lm_advanced_main (sha256 adac974b...) and libLiteRtOpenClAccelerator.so (d9dd64c3...) fetched on 2026-10-04 from storage.googleapis.com/litert/binaries/latest/android_arm64/litert_lm/ (object last-modified 2026-09-18; the binary carries the string 0.18.0 and prints no version line; LiteRT-LM main that day = 56c67f7d, the binary's own commit unconfirmed), so the snapshot axis is the digest token prebuilt-adac974b until the owner names it (DECISIONS #174(2)). Each figure is the median of the iterations of one process; per-iteration values are in metrics (iteration 1 starts cold at the full clock ceiling, later ones run under the phone's own thermal cap).
